newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stocks up for 4th day, Malbak leaps.
newsitem.headline: S.African stocks up for 4th day, Malbak leaps.

text.p: South African shares rallied for the fourth consecutive day on heavy foreign and local buying, which sent packaging stock Malbak surging and the financial and all-share indexes to fresh highs.

Dealers said that renewed talk of an interest rate cut in the third quarter of the year propped up banking shares, which together with other heavyweights also received a boost from futures-related arbitrage deals.
The financial index soared over 122 points or 1.3 percent, helping the industrial index gain 41.5 points to 8,469.9. The industrial index has put on over 220 points so far this week.
These conspired to push up the all-share index to a new high of 7,218.5, up 45.7 points and beating a previous 7,214 set on May 14.
The Johannesburg Stock Exchange also said that market capitalisation touched a record of 1,234 billion rand on Wednesday, above the 1,233 billion recorded on May 14.
Malbak also moved up on continued talk that it was set to be bought out by big industrial Remgro.
Dealers said turnover on Thursday was high at over 920 million rand, boosted by several large bookovers in both big index and smaller stocks.

Platinum stocks were chased as the white metal fixed at $440, its highest level since September 1995, but gold stocks were one of the few sectors shunned on the day as bullion slipped to near the $340 level. The index ended off 5.4 points at a fresh 50-month low of 1,140.3.
